none.rule4: target = the first opposite reversal beyond entry, no cap
none.rule4_text: Take profit at the first bearish reversal below the entry, however far away it is, there is no ceiling, so a level sitting 8R away is ridden to 8R. Rule 3 already guarantees it is at least 3.5R away. If every level below has been elected, the trade simply waits, holding, until a new one appears; the stop stays in place throughout.
none.lede: Held to the end of the move: there is no ceiling, so a trade runs to the first opposite reversal beyond entry however far away that is. Rule 3 keeps that level at least 3.5R away at entry.
none.caveat: a reversal target counts as hit whenever the day's range touches it
none.label: no cap

wick.label: entry bar wick
wick.rule4: target = one tick beyond the entry bar's own wick (a short: below its low)
wick.rule4_text: Take profit one tick below the entry bar's own low, a tick past the wick it printed on the way back down. The level is fixed the moment the trade is placed and never moves, no reversal level and no R ceiling is involved. The whole trade is contained by the entry bar: the stop one tick above its high, the target one tick below its low. This is a bet on the initial energy of the move, if the thesis behind the entry is right, that low should break more often than the high does. A winner is worth whatever the entry bar measured, which is usually well under 3.5R.
wick.lede: Captures the initial energy move only: the target is fixed at entry, one tick beyond the entry bar's own wick, a tick below its low on a short, and never moves. Stop and target are the two sides of the entry bar, so the bet is simply that its low breaks before its high.
wick.caveat: the entry bar's low counts as broken whenever the day's range touches one tick below it

close.label: bar 0 close
close.rule4: exit = the entry bar's own close, flat the same day
close.rule4_text: Close the position at the entry bar's own close. The trade is opened and shut on the same day: it fills at the first reversal and is marked out at that day's closing price, so nothing is ever carried overnight. The entry trigger requires that close to be beyond the entry price, so on gross terms this exit cannot lose, the losers are the trades whose move was smaller than the slippage charged to get in and out. The stop never trades, it is spent by the time the close confirms the entry and is here only to size the position.
close.lede: Flat by the bell: the position is closed at the entry bar's own close, the same day it was opened, so nothing is carried through the nightly session. It fills at the first reversal and is marked out at that day's closing price.
close.caveat: entry and exit both land on one daily bar, so the fill at the reversal and the fill at the close are assumed to be the same day's first and last prices

open1.label: bar 1 open
open1.rule4: exit = the open of the price bar that follows the entry bar
open1.rule4_text: Close the position at the open of the next price bar, bar 1, usually the following day. The trade is carried through one nightly session and no further. That open is the first price of the bar, so nothing can trade ahead of it and the exit is unconditional: there is no level to reach and no path to be ambiguous about. The stop never trades, it is here only to size the position, which means an adverse overnight gap takes the trade out for more than 1R.
open1.lede: Holds through one night and no longer: the position is closed at the open of bar 1, the price bar that follows the entry bar. That open is the first price of the day, so the exit is unconditional, and what the trade earns is exactly what the nightly session did to it.
open1.caveat: the whole result is the overnight move, so it rests entirely on the next bar's open being a fillable price

close1.label: bar 1 close
close1.rule4: exit = the close of the price bar that follows the entry bar
close1.rule4_text: Close the position at the close of bar 1, the price bar that follows the entry bar. The trade is carried through one nightly session and then the whole of the next day, and is marked out at that day's closing price. This is the first of these exits that gives the move a full session to work: it is not reading the open reaction, it is asking what the day made of it. The stop is live for that whole bar, and it fires ahead of the close, a stop triggers the moment price touches it while a market-on-close waits for the bell.
close1.lede: Gives the move one full day: the position is held through the night and closed at the close of bar 1, the price bar after the entry bar. The stop is live throughout that bar, so a trade that goes wrong is cut at 1R rather than carried to the bell.
close1.caveat: a stop inside bar 1's range is assumed to have been hit before that bar's close, which is true of a stop order but cannot be checked on a daily bar

open2.label: bar 2 open
open2.rule4: exit = the open of price bar 2
open2.rule4_text: Close the position at the open of bar 2, two bars after the entry bar. The trade is carried through two nightly sessions and the whole day between them. That open is the first price of its bar, so the exit itself is unconditional and nothing can trade ahead of it. The stop is live on bar 1, the full day in between, so this is Quickfixopen1 with one more day of room and a real floor under it for that day.
open2.lede: Holds through two nights and the day between them: the position is closed at the open of bar 2. The stop is live for the whole of bar 1, and only the exit bar's own open is beyond its reach.
open2.caveat: two of the three sessions are overnight moves, so the result rests on bar 2's open being a fillable price

close2.label: bar 2 close
close2.rule4: exit = the close of price bar 2
close2.rule4_text: Close the position at the close of bar 2, two bars after the entry bar. The trade is given two full sessions to work and is then marked out at the second one's closing price, so it is the longest fixed hold of these exits. The stop is live across both of those bars and fires ahead of the close on the exit bar. What this asks is whether the reaction to the entry keeps paying past the first day, or whether the move is spent by then.
close2.lede: The longest fixed hold: the position is carried through two full price bars and closed at the close of bar 2. The stop is live for both of them, so a trade that turns is cut rather than held to the second bell.
close2.caveat: a stop inside either bar's range is assumed to have been hit before that bar's close, which is true of a stop order but cannot be checked on a daily bar
